questions.q: What binds people together into a nation?
answer: A nation is a large body of people who feel that they belong together, even though most of them will never meet one another, which is why a nation is often called an imagined community.

answer.text: Above all, a nation is held together by a shared belief among its members that they form one community and wish to live together as one. It is not the physical features of people but this common conviction that makes a nation.

A nation usually shares a common history, with memories of struggles, achievements and heroes, and a sense of continuity from the past. It is also generally linked to a particular territory, a homeland that its people regard as their own.
Finally, a nation is united by shared political ideals and a common vision of the kind of society and state its members wish to build.

answer: Thus common beliefs, history, territory and aspirations together bind people into a nation.
